forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Runnymede Council's General Fund reserves forecast to fall from £21.6m to £2m by 2032
news_drafts.lead: The General Fund working balance, money set aside as a cushion against unexpected costs, is forecast to fall from £21.6m to £2.0m by 2032. Between 2029 and 2031 alone, reserves are forecast to fall by £11.7m. The Housing Revenue Account (HRA), the council's separate account for its housing stock, faces a £9.1m deficit forecast for 2026/27, reducing reserves from £25.3m to £15.0m, with ongoing annual deficits expected. The Pay and Grading review is the principal driver of General Fund deterioration, creating a £1.241m structural cost pressure. The council is exploring early repayment of one loan using maturing investments and has approved property disposals to reduce borrowing and interest payments. Accounts for 2025/26 remain unfinalized due to resourcing and introduction of a new Financial Management System, meaning opening reserve figures are indicative only.

news_drafts.headline: Runnymede reserves forecast to fall 91% by 2032 as housing account swings into deficit
news_drafts.lead: Runnymede Council's financial position deteriorated sharply at its Corporate Management Committee meeting on 24 September, with general reserves (money set aside as a cushion) forecast to collapse from £21.6m in March 2027 to £2.0m by 2032. The fall accelerates from 2029 onwards, dropping £11.7m in two years alone. The Housing Revenue Account, the ring-fenced account for the council's housing stock, recorded a £9.1m deficit in 2026/27, reducing its working balance from £25.3m to £15.0m. The council's largest income source is rental income from investment properties, generating £25.9m annually, though the council acknowledged risk from difficulty reletting at current rates. A £1.2m cost pressure from a 2025 pay and grading review is the main driver of the forecast deterioration. The council approved property disposals to reduce borrowing and interest costs and is exploring early repayment of one loan using maturing investments, moves that signal response to structural budget pressures rather than resolution of them.

news_drafts.headline: Runnymede's general fund reserves forecast to fall from £21.6m (March 2027) to £2.0m (March 2032), losing £11.7m in two years from 2029
news_drafts.lead: Runnymede's working balance — the general reserve that sits behind all its day-to-day spending — is forecast to fall from £21.6m at the end of March 2027 to just £2.0m by March 2032, the Corporate Management Committee was told on 24 September. The decline accelerates sharply from 2029 onwards: the council will lose £11.7m in reserves in the two years to 2031 alone. The principal driver is a £1.241m cost pressure from a pay and grading review completed in 2025, which creates an ongoing structural deficit. The council explicitly states that if it continues beyond the end of this financial year, further savings and efficiencies would be needed to avoid the forecast materialising. The Housing Revenue Account, which manages the council's own housing stock, faces its own pressure: it forecasts a £9.1m deficit in 2026/27, reducing its working balance to £15.0m.

findings.paper_title: 2026-27 Q1 Treasury Management Report v1 - Final
findings.headline: Investment portfolio returned 4.36% in Q1 2026-27, exceeding the 3.75% risk-free SONIA benchmark
findings.detail: The Council's investment returns, including dividends from pooled funds, outperformed the average 90-day SONIA rate by 61 basis points. This outperformance was principally driven by higher returns from longer-term investments that matured during the quarter. Investments held at quarter-end totalled £89.1m.
findings.matters: Investment returns directly contribute to treasury income budgets; outperformance against benchmark indicates effective cash management and investment strategy despite challenging market conditions.
findings.figures: Council actual return 4.36%; average 90-day SONIA benchmark 3.75%; spread 61 basis points; total investments £89.1m
findings.quote: The Council's actual interest rate performance during the first three months of 2026/27 was 4.36% (including dividends from pooled funds) which compares favourably with the average SONIA rates

findings.paper_title: 2026-27 Q1 Treasury Management Report v1 - Final
findings.headline: Council maintained under-borrowed position in Q1, using £89.1m of reserves and cash rather than external borrowing
findings.detail: No new borrowing was undertaken in the quarter. The Council deliberately did not access the PWLB or money markets, instead using its own reserves and cash balances to support operations. Total borrowings fell by £306k to £586,808k, while the Capital Financing Requirement (borrowing need) remained at £672.931m. This strategy avoids external borrowing costs but commits reserves to internal financing.
findings.matters: Choice of internal financing over external borrowing has material implications for cash position, opportunity cost, and reported net borrowing; signals Council preference for liquidity over market access during high-rate environment.
findings.figures: Investments held £89.1m; total borrowings £586,808k (down from £587,114k); CFR £672,931k; under-borrowing of £86,123k
findings.quote: No new borrowing was undertaken during the quarter meaning that the Council continued to maintain an under-borrowed position. This meant that the capital borrowing need, the CFR, was not fully funded with loan debt, as cash supporting the Council's reserves, balances and cash flow was used as an interim measure in the high interest rates environment and the period of low capital spend.

findings.paper_title: 2026-27 Q1 Treasury Management Report v1 - Final
findings.headline: Capital structure resolution at three wholly owned subsidiaries has progressed slower than anticipated and remains unfinished
findings.detail: Runnymede has loaned £41.909m to three wholly owned companies at rates from 4.22% to 7.54%. Capital structure issues identified in March 2025 are still being worked on. Progress has lagged plan and officers are currently in 'the final process of stage two' following further legal and due diligence advice. The nature of the structural issues is not disclosed.
findings.matters: Unresolved capital structure at group subsidiaries delays financial optimization and indicates ongoing complexity or resource constraints; affects group risk profile and financing strategy.
findings.figures: Loans to three subsidiaries total £41,909k: Addlestone One £25,326k at 5.04%, Magna Square £11,838k at 4.22%, Other £1,000k at 4.86%, Working Capital £3,745k at 7.36%–7.54%
findings.quote: Progress on resolving the capital structure issues has been slower than anticipated and officers are currently in the final process of stage two of the agreed actions following the receipt of further legal and due diligence advice.

findings.paper_title: 2026-27 Q1 Treasury Management Report v1 - Final
findings.headline: Proposed refinancing deal for one loan fell away in April; Council now exploring early repayment using available discounts
findings.detail: Officers presented a refinancing option to the Corporate Management Committee in April 2026, but after due diligence the offer was withdrawn. They are now pursuing an alternative approach to repay the loan in full using maturing investments and available early-repayment discounts. No details on which loan, the terms offered, or why the deal proved unviable.
findings.matters: Refinancing and early-repayment decisions directly affect future debt costs and cash-flow timing; abandoned deals indicate market conditions or commercial terms that made proceeding uneconomic.
findings.figures: Specific loan principal not disclosed (confidential); total borrowings £586,808k as of 30 June 2026
findings.quote: In April 2026, Officers presented a confidential report to the Corporate Management Committee on a potential refinancing deal for one of our loans. Having now undertaken their due diligence, this offer has fallen away. Officers are now exploring a second option which would see this loan repaid in full by utilising maturing investments and available discounts for early repayment.

findings.paper_title: CMC - Q1 Investment Property Update - Final
findings.headline: Debt service coverage ratios improved to 2.55 (interest cover) and 1.87 (total debt cover), both in safe territory.
findings.detail: Interest cover ratio improved to 2.55 from 2.46 prior year; debt coverage ratio (including MRP principal repayment) improved to 1.87 from 1.83 prior year. Document states that ratios above 1.5 are considered safe; a ratio below 1 indicates borrower struggles to meet obligations. Both metrics now comfortably exceed safety threshold, indicating net rental income continues to cover combined interest and principal obligations despite asset value declines.
findings.matters: While LTV is acutely problematic, improving coverage ratios show cash flow from operations is sufficient to service debt obligations. This demonstrates the portfolio's income remains resilient despite market stress, supporting repayment capacity despite negative equity.
findings.figures: Interest cover 2.55 (from 2.46); debt cover 1.87 (from 1.83); safe threshold noted as 1.5
findings.quote: Debt cover ratio The total net income from property investments compared to the total annual MRP and interest on associated borrowings 1.87 (Previous Year 1.83)
